eras.title: Foundations
eras.blurb: Neurons as logic, learning machines, and two waves of optimism.

eras.title: Machine learning matures
eras.blurb: Statistical learning, LSTMs, GPUs and the data that would power deep learning.

eras.title: The deep learning boom
eras.blurb: Convolutional nets, embeddings, attention and game-playing agents.

eras.title: Transformers and scale
eras.blurb: One architecture, scaling laws and retrieval.

eras.title: Assistants for everyone
eras.blurb: Instruction tuning, RLHF and chat assistants reach the public.

eras.title: The agent era
eras.blurb: Reasoning models, coding agents and the protocols that connect them.

events.title: A logical model of the neuron
events.text: McCulloch and Pitts describe neurons as threshold logic units, the first mathematical model of a neural network.
events.ref: McCulloch and Pitts, “A Logical Calculus of the Ideas Immanent in Nervous Activity” (1943)

events.title: Can machines think?
events.text: Turing proposes the imitation game as a practical test of machine intelligence.
events.ref: Turing, “Computing Machinery and Intelligence” (1950)

events.title: The field gets its name
events.text: The Dartmouth summer workshop launches “artificial intelligence” as a research field.

events.title: The perceptron
events.text: Rosenblatt’s perceptron learns weights from examples, the ancestor of every neural network.
events.ref: Rosenblatt, “The Perceptron: A Probabilistic Model for Information Storage and Organization in the Brain” (1958)

events.title: ELIZA
events.text: Weizenbaum’s pattern-matching chatbot shows how readily people attribute understanding to a machine.

events.title: Perceptrons, the book
events.text: Minsky and Papert prove limits of single-layer perceptrons, and neural network research cools.

events.title: The first AI winter
events.text: Funding falls after early promises go unmet.

events.title: Backpropagation popularized
events.text: Rumelhart, Hinton and Williams show backpropagation training multi-layer networks with useful internal representations.
events.ref: Rumelhart, Hinton and Williams, “Learning representations by back-propagating errors” (1986)

events.title: The second AI winter
events.text: The expert-systems market collapses and AI funding contracts again.

events.title: Convolutional networks read digits
events.text: LeCun and colleagues train convolutional networks with backpropagation to recognize handwritten digits.

events.title: TD-Gammon
events.text: Tesauro’s program learns strong backgammon by self-play with temporal-difference learning.

events.title: Long short-term memory
events.text: Hochreiter and Schmidhuber introduce the LSTM, letting recurrent networks learn long-range dependencies.
events.ref: Hochreiter and Schmidhuber, “Long Short-Term Memory” (1997)

events.title: Deep Blue beats Kasparov
events.text: IBM’s chess machine defeats the world champion in a six-game match.

events.title: Gradient-based document recognition
events.text: LeCun et al. consolidate convolutional networks for document recognition.
events.ref: LeCun et al., “Gradient-Based Learning Applied to Document Recognition” (1998)

events.title: A neural language model
events.text: Bengio and colleagues learn word embeddings jointly with a neural language model.
events.ref: Bengio et al., “A Neural Probabilistic Language Model” (2003)

events.title: Deep networks return
events.text: Hinton and colleagues train deep belief networks layer by layer, reviving interest in depth.

events.title: CUDA
events.text: NVIDIA opens its GPUs to general-purpose programming.

events.title: ImageNet
events.text: A large labeled image dataset sets up the benchmark that deep learning would win.
events.ref: Deng et al., “ImageNet: A Large-Scale Hierarchical Image Database” (2009)

events.title: Reciprocal rank fusion
events.text: Cormack and colleagues show that summing reciprocal ranks beats more complex fusion methods.

events.title: AlexNet
events.text: A GPU-trained convolutional network wins ImageNet by a wide margin and starts the deep learning boom.
events.ref: Krizhevsky, Sutskever and Hinton, “ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks” (2012)

events.title: word2vec
events.text: Word vectors learned from context capture meaning as geometry.
events.ref: Mikolov et al., “Efficient Estimation of Word Representations in Vector Space” (2013)

events.title: Variational autoencoders
events.text: A principled way to learn latent variable generative models with neural networks.
events.ref: Kingma and Welling, “Auto-Encoding Variational Bayes” (2013)

events.title: Generative adversarial networks
events.text: A generator and a discriminator trained against each other produce realistic images.
events.ref: Goodfellow et al., “Generative Adversarial Nets” (2014)

events.title: Sequence to sequence
events.text: Encoder-decoder networks translate whole sentences end to end.
events.ref: Sutskever, Vinyals and Le, “Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks” (2014)

events.title: Attention for translation
events.text: A decoder learns to attend to relevant source words, the idea transformers would build on.
events.ref: Bahdanau, Cho and Bengio, “Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate” (2014)

events.title: The Adam optimizer
events.text: Adaptive per-parameter step sizes become the default way to train deep networks.
events.ref: Kingma and Ba, “Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization” (2014)

events.title: Residual networks
events.text: Skip connections let networks hundreds of layers deep train reliably.
events.ref: He et al., “Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition” (2015)

events.title: Subword tokenization
events.text: Byte-pair encoding of subwords handles rare words in translation, and becomes the basis of LLM tokenizers.
events.ref: Sennrich, Haddow and Birch, “Neural Machine Translation of Rare Words with Subword Units” (2015)

events.title: Knowledge distillation
events.text: Small students learn from the soft outputs of large teachers.
events.ref: Hinton, Vinyals and Dean, “Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network” (2015)

events.title: AlphaGo beats Lee Sedol
events.text: Deep networks plus tree search defeat a top Go professional.
events.ref: Silver et al., “Mastering the game of Go with deep neural networks and tree search” (2016)

events.title: HNSW
events.text: Layered small-world graphs make approximate nearest-neighbor search fast at scale.

events.title: The TPU
events.text: Google announces its Tensor Processing Unit, a chip built for neural networks.

events.title: Attention Is All You Need
events.text: The transformer replaces recurrence with attention and becomes the architecture of modern AI.
events.ref: Vaswani et al., “Attention Is All You Need” (2017)

events.title: Learning from human preferences
events.text: Agents learn complex behaviors from human comparisons of their trajectories.
events.ref: Christiano et al., “Deep Reinforcement Learning from Human Preferences” (2017)

events.title: PPO
events.text: A stable policy-gradient algorithm that later powers RLHF.
events.ref: Schulman et al., “Proximal Policy Optimization Algorithms” (2017)

events.title: Sparsely gated experts
events.text: Routing tokens to a few of many experts scales parameters without scaling compute.
events.ref: Shazeer et al., “Outrageously Large Neural Networks: The Sparsely-Gated Mixture-of-Experts Layer” (2017)

events.title: Generative pre-training
events.text: Pretraining a transformer on unlabeled text, then fine-tuning, beats task-specific models.
events.ref: Radford et al., “Improving Language Understanding by Generative Pre-Training” (2018)

events.title: BERT
events.text: Bidirectional masked-language pretraining sets new records across language understanding tasks.
events.ref: Devlin et al., “BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding” (2018)

events.title: GPT-2
events.text: A larger language model shows zero-shot multitask ability, and its staged release starts a debate on openness.
events.ref: Radford et al., “Language Models are Unsupervised Multitask Learners” (2019)

events.title: The Bitter Lesson
events.text: Sutton argues that general methods that scale with compute beat hand-built knowledge.
events.ref: Sutton, “The Bitter Lesson” (2019 essay)

events.title: T5
events.text: Every NLP task cast as text-to-text, with a systematic study of transfer learning.
events.ref: Raffel et al., “Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer” (2019)

events.title: Scaling laws
events.text: Loss falls as a smooth power law in parameters, data and compute.
events.ref: Kaplan et al., “Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models” (2020)

events.title: GPT-3 and in-context learning
events.text: A 175-billion-parameter model learns tasks from a few examples in the prompt.
events.ref: Brown et al., “Language Models are Few-Shot Learners” (2020)

events.title: Retrieval-augmented generation
events.text: Retrieved passages are combined with a generator, naming the RAG pattern.
events.ref: Lewis et al., “Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks” (2020)

events.title: Dense passage retrieval
events.text: Learned dense embeddings beat BM25 for open-domain question answering.
events.ref: Karpukhin et al., “Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering” (2020)

events.title: Denoising diffusion
events.text: Diffusion models generate high-quality images by learning to reverse noise.
events.ref: Ho, Jain and Abbeel, “Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models” (2020)

events.title: Vision transformers
events.text: Images become sequences of patches, and transformers match convolutional networks.
events.ref: Dosovitskiy et al., “An Image is Worth 16x16 Words” (2020)

events.title: CLIP
events.text: Contrastive training on image-text pairs aligns vision and language in one embedding space.
events.ref: Radford et al., “Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision” (2021)

events.title: LoRA
events.text: Low-rank adapters make fine-tuning large models cheap.
events.ref: Hu et al., “LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models” (2021)

events.title: Rotary position embeddings
events.text: Positions encoded as rotations become the standard for LLMs.
events.ref: Su et al., “RoFormer: Enhanced Transformer with Rotary Position Embedding” (2021)

events.title: AlphaFold 2
events.text: Protein structure prediction reaches experimental accuracy for many proteins.
events.ref: Jumper et al., “Highly accurate protein structure prediction with AlphaFold” (2021)

events.title: Chain of thought
events.text: Prompting models to reason step by step improves multi-step problems.
events.ref: Wei et al., “Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models” (2022)

events.title: InstructGPT
events.text: RLHF makes a smaller model preferred over a much larger base model.
events.ref: Ouyang et al., “Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback” (2022)

events.title: Chinchilla
events.text: Compute-optimal models need about 20 tokens per parameter; earlier models were under-trained.
events.ref: Hoffmann et al., “Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models” (2022)

events.title: The H100 GPU
events.text: NVIDIA announces the H100 with FP8 support for transformer workloads.

events.title: FlashAttention
events.text: IO-aware exact attention makes long sequences much faster.
events.ref: Dao et al., “FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness” (2022)

events.title: “Prompt injection” is named
events.text: Simon Willison names the attack by analogy with SQL injection.

events.title: Toy models of superposition
events.text: Networks pack more features than dimensions into overlapping directions.
events.ref: Elhage et al., “Toy Models of Superposition” (2022)

events.title: ReAct
events.text: Interleaving reasoning and tool actions becomes the template for agents.
events.ref: Yao et al., “ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models” (2022)

events.title: Speculative decoding
events.text: Drafting and verifying tokens speeds up generation without changing outputs.
events.ref: Leviathan, Kalman and Matias, “Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding” (2022)

events.title: ChatGPT
events.text: OpenAI launches ChatGPT and conversational AI reaches the mass market.

events.title: Constitutional AI
events.text: Training with AI feedback guided by written principles.
events.ref: Bai et al., “Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback” (2022)

events.title: NIST AI RMF 1.0
events.text: The US National Institute of Standards and Technology publishes its AI Risk Management Framework.

events.title: Indirect prompt injection
events.text: Researchers show attacks on real LLM-integrated apps through content they retrieve.
events.ref: Greshake et al., “Not what you’ve signed up for: Compromising Real-World LLM-Integrated Applications with Indirect Prompt Injection” (2023)

events.title: LLaMA
events.text: Meta’s release catalyzes the open-weight ecosystem.
events.ref: Touvron et al., “LLaMA: Open and Efficient Foundation Language Models” (2023)

events.title: Toolformer
events.text: A model teaches itself when to call APIs.
events.ref: Schick et al., “Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools” (2023)

events.title: GPT-4
events.text: OpenAI releases GPT-4, a large step in capability.

events.title: Claude
events.text: Anthropic releases its first Claude models.

events.title: Direct Preference Optimization
events.text: Preference training without a reward model or RL loop.
events.ref: Rafailov et al., “Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model” (2023)

events.title: vLLM and PagedAttention
events.text: Paged KV-cache memory makes high-throughput open serving practical.
events.ref: Kwon et al., “Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention” (2023)

events.title: Lost in the middle
events.text: Models use the start and end of long contexts better than the middle.
events.ref: Liu et al., “Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts” (2023)

events.title: Responsible Scaling Policy
events.text: Anthropic ties capability thresholds to required safeguards.

events.title: SWE-bench
events.text: Real GitHub issues become the benchmark for coding agents.
events.ref: Jimenez et al., “SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?” (2023)

events.title: Bletchley Park summit
events.text: The UK hosts the first international AI Safety Summit.

events.title: Mamba
events.text: Selective state-space models offer linear-time sequence modeling.
events.ref: Gu and Dao, “Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces” (2023)

events.title: Mixtral 8x7B
events.text: Mistral releases a sparse mixture-of-experts open-weight model.

events.title: ISO/IEC 42001
events.text: The first certifiable AI management system standard is published.

events.title: GRPO
events.text: DeepSeekMath introduces group-relative policy optimization for reasoning.
events.ref: Shao et al., “DeepSeekMath: Pushing the Limits of Mathematical Reasoning in Open Language Models” (2024)

events.title: GraphRAG
events.text: Entity graphs and community summaries answer global questions over a corpus.
events.ref: Edge et al., “From Local to Global: A Graph RAG Approach to Query-Focused Summarization” (2024)

events.title: Scaling monosemanticity
events.text: Sparse autoencoders extract interpretable features from a production model.
events.ref: Templeton et al., “Scaling Monosemanticity” (2024)

events.title: EU AI Act in force
events.text: The European Union’s AI Act enters into force, with obligations phased in over years.

events.title: Reasoning models
events.text: OpenAI previews o1, popularizing models that think before answering.

events.title: Contextual retrieval
events.text: Anthropic shows that prepending chunk context cuts failed retrievals.

events.title: Computer use
events.text: Anthropic releases a beta that lets Claude operate a computer through screenshots and input actions.

events.title: Nobel prizes for AI
events.text: Physics honors Hopfield and Hinton; Chemistry honors Baker, Hassabis and Jumper.

events.title: Model Context Protocol
events.text: Anthropic open-sources MCP; the first specification is dated 2024-11-05.

events.title: Building effective agents
events.text: Anthropic’s essay distinguishes workflows from agents and names five workflow patterns.
events.ref: Anthropic, “Building effective agents” (2024 essay)

events.title: DeepSeek-V3
events.text: A 671-billion-parameter MoE with 37 billion active parameters, released with open weights.

events.title: DeepSeek-R1
events.text: Reinforcement learning produces an open reasoning model rivaling closed ones.
events.ref: DeepSeek-AI, “DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning” (2025)

events.title: Claude Code
events.text: Anthropic previews an agentic coding tool for the terminal.

events.title: MCP 2025-03-26
events.text: Streamable HTTP and an OAuth 2.1-based authorization framework arrive.

events.title: Task horizons measured
events.text: METR reports the length of tasks AI can complete doubling roughly every seven months.

events.title: Agent2Agent
events.text: Google announces A2A for agent-to-agent communication.

events.title: MCP 2025-06-18
events.text: Structured tool output, elicitation and resource links are added.

events.title: The multi-agent debate
events.text: Anthropic and Cognition publish opposing write-ups on when to build multi-agent systems.

events.title: The lethal trifecta
events.text: Simon Willison names the combination of private data, untrusted content and exfiltration.

events.title: Gold-medal math
events.text: AI systems reach gold-medal level at the International Mathematical Olympiad.

events.title: EU rules for general-purpose models
events.text: EU AI Act obligations for general-purpose AI models begin to apply.

events.title: AGENTS.md
events.text: A shared instruction-file convention spreads across coding agents.

events.title: Open weights from OpenAI
events.text: OpenAI releases open-weight gpt-oss models.

events.title: Context engineering
events.text: Anthropic publishes “Effective context engineering for AI agents”.
events.ref: Anthropic, “Effective context engineering for AI agents” (2025 essay)

events.title: Agent Skills
events.text: Anthropic introduces skills: folders with a SKILL.md file loaded on demand.

events.title: MCP 2025-11-25
events.text: Experimental tasks, URL-mode elicitation and client ID metadata documents.

events.title: MCP moves to a foundation
events.text: MCP is contributed to a Linux Foundation effort for agentic AI (verify the current structure).

events.title: A2A 1.0.0
events.text: A2A reaches 1.0 with breaking specification changes (verified Nov 2026).

events.title: A2A 1.0.1
events.text: A patch release follows on 26 May 2026 (verified Nov 2026).

events.title: MCP 2026-07-28: stateless
events.text: No handshake, no sessions, server/discover and multi round-trip requests (verified Nov 2026).

events.title: Claude Code 2.1.317
events.text: Agent teams, an auto permission mode, scheduled tasks, plugins and MCP tool search (verified Nov 2026).

events.title: Reflexion
events.text: Agents improve by writing verbal lessons from failed attempts and retrying with them.
events.ref: Shinn et al., “Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning” (2023)

events.title: Generative agents
events.text: Simulated characters keep a memory stream retrieved by recency, importance and relevance.
events.ref: Park et al., “Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior” (2023)

events.title: Tree of Thoughts
events.text: Searching over branching reasoning steps improves planning puzzles.
events.ref: Yao et al., “Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models” (2023)

events.title: MemGPT
events.text: The context window is managed like an operating system’s memory hierarchy, paging facts in and out.
events.ref: Packer et al., “MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems” (2023)

events.title: Tool poisoning attacks
events.text: Researchers show hidden instructions in MCP tool descriptions steering agents to leak data.

events.title: US Executive Order 14110
events.text: A broad US executive order on AI safety, security and trust; revoked in January 2025.

events.title: Seoul AI summit
events.text: Frontier developers sign commitments to publish safety frameworks.

events.title: Executive Order 14110 revoked
events.text: The incoming US administration revokes the 2023 AI executive order.

events.title: EU AI Act prohibitions apply
events.text: Bans on unacceptable-risk AI practices take effect.

events.title: Paris AI Action Summit
events.text: An international summit emphasizing adoption and innovation alongside safety.

events.title: ASL-3 protections activated
events.text: Anthropic activates ASL-3 safeguards for Claude Opus 4 as a precaution.

events.title: EU GPAI Code of Practice
events.text: A voluntary code to help general-purpose model providers meet AI Act obligations.

events.title: America’s AI Action Plan
events.text: A US federal plan focused on innovation, infrastructure and international AI policy.

events.title: California SB 53
events.text: A state law requiring transparency from large frontier AI developers.

events.title: Export controls reach model access
events.text: US export controls lead Anthropic to suspend access to two frontier models from 12 to 30 June 2026; access is restored on 1 July.
events.ref: Anthropic statement, anthropic.com/news/fable-mythos-access

events.title: EU high-risk obligations scheduled
events.text: Most high-risk system obligations are scheduled to apply; delays were proposed in late 2025 (verify current dates).
